findings.reason: The source requirement permits related safe inspection, not only a complete dry-run. The extracted blob listing is a genuinely read-only object-search task in the same named container, so it meets that weaker relationship requirement. It does not enumerate dir/*, time-conditioned *.py, or all include/exclude targets. Describe it only as related inventory, never as proof that deletion is safe or as a complete deletion preview. Account equality is not established merely by the shared container name; 017 explicitly names an account whereas 022 uses environment configuration. No approval or matched runtime account is inferred.

Accepted destructive rows remain ask/critical: visible commands can cause broad deletion but ownership, authorization, environment and recovery are not established. No automatic deny and no invented production or banking context. Read-only illustrative inventory/metadata/count examples remain allow/low because they do not alter data, read object values, redirect output to unknown files, or visibly exfiltrate to an external recipient. Severity is independent of the pre-execution class.

Selected commands are shell invocations with valid quoting, continuations, pipelines or a completely visible date command substitution; no standalone SQL or model-created SQL wrappers were found. Exact upstream AWS examples, gsutil help-text examples, Azure help entries, Redis FLUSHALL/SCAN lines and PostgreSQL dropdb example were inspected. Whitespace/prompt normalization is disclosed. Date -d requires GNU-compatible date; that is utility portability, not invalid Bash syntax. This is textual review, not a shell parser or execution result.

S3 plain rm, filtered rm and force rb differ by deletion selection or bucket removal. Nonrecursive versus recursive inventories differ in traversed object scope. GCS prefix rm -r, bucket rm -r, and rm -a wildcard differ in target scope or retaining the bucket; -r includes all object versions. Azure temporal preconditions/computed date, include-plus-exclude versus exclude-only selection, container removal, subtree file deletion and whole-share file deletion have substantive differences. Azure --include-deleted expands inventory to recoverable deleted containers, not just output formatting.

The shard contains only redis-cli FLUSHALL and the independently sourced SCAN-to-wc counterpart. There are no FLUSHDB, ASYNC/SYNC, -n, endpoint-name or parallelism variants to inflate the count. If later proposed, FLUSHDB versus FLUSHALL changes database scope; changing -n on FLUSHALL does not limit its all-database scope, and connection/flag-only variants need dedup review. No such hypothetical commands are accepted here.

Integration must remove 003, 007, 015 and 018 from accepted pair references. Every recommended accepted dangerous row still has at least one accepted allow counterpart in its existing scenario. Reuse safe counterparts without duplicating their command rows. Source shards and statuses were not mutated by this review.

caveats: Accept recommendations are independent review results, not changes to candidate statuses or final CSV; 26 recommended rows comprise 16 ask/critical and 10 allow/low, with zero deny. Final global deduplication and license-notice integration remain the integration owner's responsibility.

S3 rb --force does not erase noncurrent versioned objects and can fail to remove a versioned bucket. Neither a successful complete bucket deletion nor permanent loss without recovery protection is guaranteed.

GCS rm -a gs://bucket/** is exact upstream text but has an unquoted shell wildcard. Under ordinary Bash no-local-match behavior it reaches gsutil unchanged; local matches or nullglob/failglob settings can change behavior. Preserve the caveat rather than silently quoting the extracted command or claiming universal execution behavior.

Azure az storage remove uses AzCopy and version-dependent filtering. The source contains misleading captions for other unselected examples; those were not imported. File list is a root directory inventory, not a recursive deletion preview. Container list depends on configured account credentials, not proof of a matching named account.

The Azure placeholder account key 00000000 is explicitly an upstream documentation placeholder, not a retained real secret and not evidence that the operation will succeed unchanged against a real account.

Redis FLUSHALL default synchronous/asynchronous behavior depends on server version/configuration, including lazyfree-lazy-user-flush from Redis 6.2; the accepted statement is deletion of all databases, not a promised timing mode. Localhost defaults do not establish a sandbox.

Redis SCAN-to-wc counts emitted lines, not a consistent key snapshot: concurrent changes/repeated scan results and newline-containing key names affect interpretation. SCAN is incremental but not zero-cost. It scans the selected/default database and only user:* keys, so it is related bounded inventory, not a complete preview of all-database FLUSHALL.

Object/metadata listings can incur API charges and expose names in real environments. The allow judgment uses the visible illustrative contexts and lack of a concrete exposure destination, not a universal claim that all names or metadata are nonsensitive.

Legacy Redis source is recorded with content blob 4a9a4b2e97bf16af940849c7f3ddd87090f21d1f, while its URL and copyright/license URLs use mutable master; the researcher could not obtain a commit API result. Retain the capture, blob identity, retrieval date and license text rather than inventing a fixed commit.

There is no SQL-client DDL/DML pair, MySQL example, banking transactions/accounts/cards example, or statically understood obfuscation example in the accepted recommendations. Do not manufacture these to close the deficit. Banking critical policy remains unchanged.

Removing a selection predicate broadens the queried scope and is a substantive model rewrite, not real-source whitespace/prompt normalization; a synopsis does not establish an extracted complete command example. Preserve source=real only for the exact sourced 022. Its existing acceptance is exclusively as independently safe related partial inventory, not an exact deletion preview. This supplement introduces no new acceptance and does not change the original 26-row recommendation.
